card werk-hmr  [decided]
Rebuild werk's dev server on a stack with HMR that survives its own edits
why: Research, two rounds of real-app testing, and a direct repro of the one open correctness concern settle it. Two priorities settle the rest: productionization and upgrade risk. See #werk-hmr:src0 through src5, and options opt1/opt2.
subtree: 4 cards, 4 decided

The agent's job includes editing werk's own source. A restart-based reload cannot support that: it kills the live claude child mid-turn every time the agent saves a file it is working through. Needs a stack where a code edit reloads the changed module without killing the process holding open child sessions.

Research (#werk-hmr:src0): vite-node invalidates transitively, not globally. Bun --hot guarantees the global object survives. Deno --watch-hmr names an in-flight async function as a forced-full-restart case, the exact shape of werk's failure. Node core has no HMR.

Toy prototype (#werk-hmr:src1): a minimal harness shaped like werk's agent, pinned on the global object, survived edits to both a sibling module and the pinned module itself, under both bun --hot and vite-node --watch.

Real-app test, unpatched (#werk-hmr:src2): werk's real code has neither guard. vite-node --watch crashed outright on an unrelated-file edit (an EADDRINUSE retry loop, then exit code 1). bun --hot did not crash, but silently orphaned a live task on the same edit.

Fix, real-app test, patched (#werk-hmr:src3): one guard clause in the server's start-up (a check, kept on the global object, that the server is not already running in this process) fixed both candidates identically. Both survive a real in-flight task through a source edit, verified with a fresh-connection check. Side effect worth knowing: this guard also means a hot reload stops applying code changes inside the start-up code - the tradeoff is 'my live session survives an edit' over 'my latest route-handler edit is live', which is correct for the original problem.

Runtime research (#werk-hmr:src4, Sept 2026): general research flagged one concrete objection to Bun as werk's runtime - oven-sh/bun #7716/#13811, open issues about SSE 'close' not firing reliably on client disconnect, which sounded like it hit werk's server directly.

Direct repro (#werk-hmr:src5): tested against Bun 1.4.1 specifically (the exact version used throughout, and the one the research flagged as the big Zig-to-Rust rewrite). Added a probe to werk's actual live-stream handler and disconnected SSE clients both cleanly and via kill -9. close fired correctly every time, the client left the server's client list, no leak. The bug is real and filed, but does not reproduce for werk's specific pattern.

Decided: move werk's runtime to Bun (bun --hot). The one concrete correctness objection did not reproduce on werk's own code on the exact version tested (1.4.1). The remaining Bun tradeoffs are a values call, not a correctness one, and two priorities resolve them: bun build --compile is a real asset for productionizing werk as a shipped tool (Node's own SEA docs mark it 'Stability: 1.1 - Active development', a weaker position), and Bun's faster breaking-change cadence is an acceptable cost given agents do the upgrade work rather than a single unaided maintainer. #werk-hmr:opt2 records staying on Node as the rejected alternative; #werk-hmr:opt1 records the original Bun rejection, superseded once #werk-hmr:src5 tested it directly.
